Author: @gilliantohver3225
Comment:
This is tonic immobility. It happens in many animals - domesticated birds, possums, and sharks being very famous examples - when the animal is totally convinced it is about to die. A last ditch method to try to avoid pain or possibly trauma. It can last from 30 seconds to 30 minutes before dissipating. You can wake a chicken from it by clapping your hands a few times or turning them away from the line (it may take a minute for the chicken to switch out of its catatonic state).

The rooster is not hypnotized or asleep. The people unknowingly scared it into catatonia (hence why it bit him right away after waking - it was stressed from what he did to it).

The Smithsonian Science Institute and National Geographic websites have good articles on this phenomenon.

Author: @OlaNordmann100
Comment: For those wondering why the line triggers tonic immobility in the rooster: One theory is that the rooster thinks the ditch that’s being drawn by the finger moving away from itself, is actually formed by its own beak, as in being dragged away by a preditor. From our point of reference we see it as the rooster being held stationary and the finger moving, but from the rooster’s point of reference, it sees it as the finger being stationary, and itself being dragged away from the finger. Being held down and having its beak in the sand probably helps the illusion. Hope this makes sense.
